HOLY c- these are a godsend. I unknowingly bought a new ge stainless steel electric range with the sensi temp coils which everyone hates and now I see why. GE legally says they cant be replaced with regular but its just liability/legal jargon. They can indeed be replaced with this. I went to homedepot before going here and 1 small size element was $29 and the larger was $35 at the time for the regular GE elements without sensitemp. The fact this is a fullset of 4 for the price of basically 1.5 of the regular ones, its worth it.

Now theres a small downside which isnt a deal breaker. The Y bracket the coil sits on doesnt have all coils clipped onto it, the coils are somewhat floating over it and only held onto by the end ring but its not a problem when something is on it. The other thing is my larger element was not centered. Like i fit it in and the base fit perfectly but the coil rings were off to the left. Still works as it should but have to align pans to the coil location and not presume middle of the under drip pan is where the middle of the coil is.

That being said Im free of sensi temp elements and can finally boil water without the stove shutting itself off. Thanks GE for being lazy and not integrating sensitemp into the actual unit with digital signals but just modded the elements of the stove making it completely backwards compatible with these elements.

These range top stove elements burner kits made my life so much easier. When they arrived, I couldn't wait to get them installed. They all snapped in very easily and worked perfectly when I turned the burners on. The original sensi-temp burners that came with the stove were perhaps one of the worst ideas I have ever seen. It took 45 minutes to boil water for pasta with the burner on high, which is ridiculous. It stayed on high for perhaps a minute or two and then then burner would go dark for at least 5-10 minutes and then start the cycle all over again. Had I known about these sensi-temp burners before I purchased this electric stove I may have opted for a gas stove. Now, I am all for saftey, but I have been cooking with an electric range for over thirty years and I never had an issue with starting a fire or whatever the reason for mandating something so impractical. This is not a cook stove, it is perhaps a stove for warming things. I will never buy another GE appliance because of this. Thanks again to  Kitchen Elements for having these burner elements available. Plus they are made in the USA.

In 2018 the UL mandated all electric stoves have must have burners with thermostats on each burner. As a result, you can't get the burners hot enough to boil water or stay lit. Buying a new stove wont solve the problem, but these do. Suggestion #2 buy the same brand replacement burner pans to help insure the burners nest right.
